proposal:
STATUS. Nothing was executed; every statement is a hand derivation from the supplied code. No polynomial-SAT claim.

A. AUDIT.
1. compression._verify_certificate: every dense clause enters `blocks`; slices are tied by sum(counts)=len(quotient); used forms are masked to the block. Equality on all 2^|support| local points gives F(x)=Q(Px) globally, and the entrywise P*L=I check gives surjectivity. I found no soundness defect and no omitted block.
2. prune cannot delete two states against each other: states are subsumption-minimal canon outputs, so mutual `below` forces equality.
3. Uncapped discovery cost: the candidate sort makes up to S*B membership tests (S<=16384, B<=1024), and the greedy loop rebuilds basis(chosen+[v]) from scratch, O(S*r^2). Neither is counted in max_verification_work. This is sound; incremental echelon insertion gives O(S*r).
4. Quotient numbering is the greedy sort index. For Neon58 I derive forms 1..12 = x1..x12 and 13..16 = x13^x14, x15^x16, x17^x18, x19^x20. The pairs are (1,9),(3,11),(5,13),(7,15) | (2,10),(4,12),(6,14),(8,16), so ascending order splits every pair and interleaves the sides.
5. step is cached on the pre-canon state, so equal canonical inputs re-run IALH.

B. TRACE THEOREM (hand proof; needs independent check). T_{r,s} has A-pairs (a_i,a_i'), i<=r, and B-pairs, j<=s; N_A is the 2^r negative transversal clauses, N_B likewise; positives are a_i|a_i'|b_j|b_j'. Branch A pair by pair.
L1 (collapse). Setting a_p=1 turns each clause ~a_p|R into R, which subsumes ~a_p'|R, and satisfies row p. canon returns exactly T_{r-1,s}, and a_p' disappears. From the a_p=0 child, a_p'=1 gives the same clause set, hence the same canonical tuple.
L2 (zero branch). a_p=a_p'=0 leaves b_j|b_j', which subsume all other rows: Z_s = pair clauses + N_B. For s<=5 an N_B support is an IALH window and every tuple UP-conflicts (a zero forces its partner, then the correspondingly flipped clause is falsified): empty table. For every s, size-nonincreasing DP refutes Z_s: eliminating b_j gives 2^(s-1) resolvents for 2^(s-1)+1 removed clauses, and the remaining complete sign cube halves at each step.
L3 (no interference). For r,s>=3 no DP step is admissible in T_{r,s} or in the a_p=0 child, since s*2^(r-1) > s+2^(r-1) and its analogues hold. At r=2, a=1 yields units plus Z_s; a=0 is DP-refutable (last pair's two variables, then the open partner).
Consequence for r,s>=3: retained layers (2,1)^(r-2),0; peak 2; 5r-7 IALH calls with only 2r distinct canonical inputs. IALH can only remove more states, so peak<=2 regardless. For r=s=4 this gives layers [2,1,2,1,0], 13 calls, 8 distinct, which is a sharper check of the trusted peak-2 run.

C. RESTRICTED FACTORING WITHOUT A QUOTIENT. Let Q be any CNF over e_1..e_t and F its OR-expansion: e_i becomes the disjunction of a private literal set M_i, and ~e_i becomes one negated member per clause, over all choices. L1 holds verbatim. Once any member of M_i is true, canon(F|alpha) is the canonical expansion of Q|e_i=1; if all are false it is that of Q|e_i=0. So at module boundaries the states are canonical expansions of restrictions of Q, and inside a module there are at most twice as many. Soundness is trivial: only the order changes, so no certificate is needed. The restriction is real: syntactic expansions only, and only while DP accepts nothing on retained states.

D. ORDER RULE (unimplemented): closing-first. At each layer branch on the variable minimising |prune(children)|, ties by id; this costs <=2n|S| memoised step calls per layer. On T_{r,s} with any numbering, the partner of an open pair gives 1 child and every other variable gives >=2, so the rule closes pairs. Independent-test prediction: peak 2 on the Neon58 quotient with its own ids, and on the canonical 20-variable input after compression.

E. WORK INEQUALITY (hand estimate). Clause count never grows (restrict, canon, SCC, admissible DP) and width is <=n. With the fixed IALH caps a step costs O(n^3 m^4) literal operations in the worst case, because each rejected DP attempt canonicalises up to m^2/4 resolvents with quadratic subsumption; HNF matrices have cap-bounded size. prune costs O(P^2 m^2 n). The total is O(n^4 m^4 P + n^2 m^2 P^2) times log n bits, with P<=2*peak (times n under rule D). So P is the only possibly superpolynomial quantity. For T_k in pair order I get O(m^2 log^5 m). Pigeonhole h=4 (peak 1, about 1.2 s per IALH call) is a constant-factor problem: memoise refute on the canonical input.

F. WHAT IT CANNOT DO. For UNSAT inputs every residual is semantically false, so no semantic width exists. Peak counts residuals that canon+IALH-5+nonincreasing DP fails to refute and that are syntactically incomparable. Extras touching module members individually, e.g. (~a_t|c_t),(~a_t'|d_t) with c_t,d_t constrained elsewhere, make completions incomparable; I conjecture 2^t states, untested. Modules that do not collapse after one more variable (majority, uncompressed parity) are invisible to rule D. Pigeonhole, ordering (Neon57, peak 4) and random 3-CNF have no modules.
missing_theorem:
MT1 (finite, Lean-sized): (a) canon(S u S+)=canon(S) whenever every clause of S+ is subsumed by a clause of S; (b) Z_s is refuted by admissible DP for every s; (c) the admissibility inequalities of L3. Together these give B for all r,s>=3.
MT2: the work inequality E as a theorem about the pinned code, including 'clause count never exceeds the input' and the cap-bounded HNF sizes. Every total-work question then reduces to P.
MT3 (open; the real gap): expansion-commutation. Prove or refute: for every CNF Q, every OR/AND-expansion F and the closing-first rule, peak(F) <= 2*peak(Q under the induced order), even when DP accepts steps on retained states. C proves this only when DP is idle. DP may eliminate a module member mid-module, and I have no invariant for that case.
MT4 (not conjectured true): a polynomial bound on closing-first P for arbitrary CNF would give P=NP. The honest target is a class theorem: characterise the extras X for which P(T_k and X) stays polynomial. I expect exactly those X whose restrictions under module completions are pairwise `below`-comparable, which is a syntactic, not a semantic, condition.
self_attack:
1. This is an ordering result. Width collapse under a module-consecutive order is the standard OBDD/formula-caching phenomenon, and earlier rounds proposed reordering and module projection. What I add is the code-level proof, the expansion statement and a detector-free rule, not a new inference.
2. The trace is a hand simulation. I checked UP tables and DP admissibility by reasoning, not execution. IALH may refute more than I found; that can only lower the profile. For s=3 I expect extra equality rows (a_p'=1; a=0 in T_{2,3}) going through the rank-deficient HNF path, which I assumed behaves as in routine runs.
3. Rule D multiplies work by n and sees one step ahead. It is not monotone under extras, unlike last round's additive vivification. The two are complementary, and neither bounds general SAT.
4. E is polynomial times P^2 and says nothing about P. Pigeonhole h=5 timing out while DPLL takes 0.13 s shows constants matter more than peak there; memoisation removes at most the repeated fraction.
5. The fixture is the rectangular T_{5,3}, not the canonical square. I estimate the square k=5 case (same predicted profile, 18 IALH calls on 89 clauses) to run near the 20 s limit. A match confirms L1-L3 beyond the trusted k=4 run; it does not test rule D or extras. Secondary predictions, lower confidence: layers [2,1,2,1,2,1,0]; counting.calls 18, refutations 5; compression skipped (all_variables_in_odd_blocks); core no_clauses_removed.
mechanism_signature: Implicit nonlinear factoring by subsumption-collapse: under module-consecutive (closing-first) branching, canon makes every nonzero completion of an OR-module the same canonical residual, so the layered solver simulates the factored formula at width times 2 with no quotient or certificate. Total work is poly(n,m) times P^2.
delta_from_prior: Round 111 learned implied sub-clauses (anchored vivification); rounds 104-110 proposed named detectors, quotients or orders. This round adds no inference and no detector. New: (1) a code-level trace theorem for all T_{r,s} that explains the trusted peak-2 observation, with layer profile, call counts and which component refutes the zero branch (DP for every s, IALH only for s<=5); (2) the OR-expansion statement, i.e. factoring done by the existing canon subsumption once the order is right; (3) a closing-first order rule driven by measured child counts rather than structure detection; (4) a work inequality isolating P, which exposes rejected DP attempts as the dominant polynomial cost; (5) audit findings: uncapped discovery cost and the quotient-order artifact behind Neon58's peak 8.
